details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1330-1562 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Six steps from the heal job, including the heavy "Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)", now run in tests-hooks-and-orchestrator (timeout-minutes: 20). That job had already reached 15m32s on run 43220859648 (#9391).
  WHY: Both reviewers rated this MAJOR (mapped to high). The change moves the overrun into the job budget-watch flags most often. On a cold runner that job can hit its 20-minute timeout, which turns CI red with no code fault and restarts the budget-watch cycle the issue is meant to end.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:Multiple lines (moved steps) | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR introduces failing contract tests: tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py, tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py and tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py.
  WHY: The reviewer rated this BLOCKER (mapped to critical) and says these tests depend on job structure, so moving the steps breaks their assumptions (job permissions, environment setup, sharding). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash checked this claim and rejected it: the tests only check their own file name or settings/scope, and the failures do not reproduce on the PR head.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1330-1562 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The copied #8208 provenance comment at lines 1359-1363 says "This job has had no steps moved in since #7690". That is false in tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, which received moved-in steps in #8993, #9078/#9046 and this PR.
  WHY: All three reviewers rated this NIT (mapped to low). There is no runtime failure, but the next budget-watch mover reads this decision record to pick a target job and would be misled. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 chose not to raise it because the paragraph at lines 1365-1367 re-scopes the comment.
- tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py:1982-2046 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The constant RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID (line 1982) now points at "tests-hooks-and-orchestrator", but it and the methods test_each_step_is_owned_only_by_the_heal_job (line 2017) and test_moved_steps_run_after_the_heal_job_setup (line 2046) still say "heal".
  WHY: Both reviewers rated this NIT (mapped to low). It is naming drift with no functional failure, and it could send a future maintainer to the wrong job. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 consider keeping the names mandated by §10 and documented at lines 1981 and 2000-2004.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Move its slowest steps (see the run's step timings) into the CI job with the most headroom, unchanged, keeping job and step names."
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/ci.yml: the target-job choice (tests-hooks-and-orchestrator) and its justification comment at lines 1330-1339, plus HEAL_9420_TARGET_JOB_ID in tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py (line 4448)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Neither ci.yml lines 1330-1339 nor changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md cites a headroom comparison or measured step timings; the comment says the pick is "an estimate ... not a measurement", ci.yml's own provenance comments show tests-hooks-and-orchestrator flagged repeatedly (#9391 15m32s at lines 3850-3851, #9078 15m33s, #8281 15m27s at lines 2805-2806, #7798 at lines 3547-3548, #7366 at lines 1789-1790, #8179 15m01s) against a 20-minute timeout (line 715), other jobs (tests-promote-stall-and-review last at #8466; tests-system-python, tests-sandbox-python, tests-sync-quick never) carry no recent flag. All four reviewers rated this MAJOR; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash disputes it because at least eight prior moves used the same estimate basis and the head's CI run was green.
- requirement: "agents.d/*": an agents.d/ fragment listed in the task's files_touched scope, per CLAUDE.md §30 ("Never add to `agents.md` (or `AGENTS.md`) directly. Write a fragment instead.")
  expected_change_site: agents.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The PR adds changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md but no agents.d/ fragment. None of the 58 existing agents.d/ fragments covers #9420/#9686/#9684, while precedent PR #9559 shipped both a changelog.d/ and an agents.d/ fragment. The pre-push gate reports tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py and tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py failing. Both reviewers rated this BLOCKER. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash reject it: files_touched permits agents.d/* but does not require it, prior step moves (#8993, #9018, #9045, #9391) used only a changelog.d/ fragment, and test_instructions_point_at_fragments (tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py:74-82) does not cover this diff.
- requirement: "Six steps … now run at the end of `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`" (changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md line 1)
  expected_change_site: MovedHeal9420StepsContractTest in tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py (test_moved_steps_run_after_setup_in_their_original_order, lines 4521-4531)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The test asserts only that the six steps come after "Install Python CI dependencies" and stay in their original order, not that they are the last six steps of the job, so a step appended later would contradict the changelog without failing any test. Both reviewers rated this NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:Lines 1330-1562 (job header at lines 708-715, timeout-minutes: 20) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Six steps go to tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, the job budget-watch has flagged most often and most recently: #9391 at 15m32s (run 43220859648, lines 3850-3851), #8281 at 15m27s (lines 2805-2806), #7798 at 15m06s (lines 3547-3548), #7366 at 15m09s (lines 1789-1790), #9078 at 15m33s. Three of the steps are heavy: "Release CI gate tests" (24 run_case calls, a polling case), "Validation shell-quoting and credential-scrub tests" (six modules in three interpreter launches) and "Cancelled CI sweep recovery tests".
  WHY: The job was already at about 15.5 of its 20 minutes. The overrun moves from the heal job to the hooks job, the budget-watch cycle reopens, and on a cold runner the job risks a timeout cancellation that turns CI red with no code fault. Steps were moved out of this same job for exactly this reason in #7366 (lines 1789-1799).
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  Requirement: "Move its slowest steps (see the run's step timings) into the CI job with the most headroom, unchanged, keeping job and step names."
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, in the choice of target job and the justification comment at lines 1330-1339. The same choice is repeated in HEAL_9420_TARGET_JOB_ID in tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py (line 4448).
  Evidence of absence: Nothing in the PR shows that tests-hooks-and-orchestrator has the most headroom; ci.yml's provenance comments say it has the least (#9391, #9078, #8281, #7798, #7366). Other jobs have no recent flag (tests-promote-stall-and-review last at #8466, lines 1261-1262; tests-system-python, tests-sandbox-python and tests-sync-quick never). The comment and changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md both say the step timings were not read, and neither gives a headroom comparison or a measured timing.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:Multiple lines (moved steps) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR introduces several failing contract tests: tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py, tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py and tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py.
  WHY: These tests appear sensitive to job structure, so moving the steps into tests-hooks-and-orchestrator has violated assumptions they rely on (job permissions, environment setup, test sharding).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:tests-hooks-and-orchestrator job (timeout-minutes 20) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The target job already has very little headroom (15m32s on run 43220859648, #9391).
  WHY: Adding six steps, including the 24-invocation scripts/release_ci_gate.sh, raises the risk of hitting the 20-minute timeout on a cold runner, which turns CI red for a non-code fault.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1330-1562 (comments above moved steps) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Copied comments such as "This job has had no steps moved in since #7690" are false for tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, which received steps in #9078, #8993 and this PR (#9684).
  WHY: This misleads future maintainers looking for headroom into targeting this job again.
- tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py:1982, 2017, 2046 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID and related methods (e.g. "test_each_step_is_owned_only_by_the_heal_job") are misnomers now that the target is the hooks job.
  WHY: The test naming drifts from the implementation, which makes maintenance more error-prone.
- TASK_GAP | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  Requirement: "agents.d/*" (an agents.d/ fragment must be added for documentation updates as per §30)
  Expected change site: agents.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md
  Evidence of absence: The PR adds a changelog fragment but no agents.d/ fragment, which was explicitly listed in the approved files_touched list.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  Requirement: "Move its slowest steps ... into the CI job with the most headroom"
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Evidence of absence: Nothing in the diff or PR metadata shows that tests-hooks-and-orchestrator (15m32s of 20m) has more headroom than other jobs.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  Requirement: "Six steps ... now run at the end of `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`" (changelog claim)
  Expected change site: `MovedHeal9420StepsContractTest` in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`
  Evidence of absence: The test checks only "after setup, in original order", not that the steps are the last ones in the job.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py:line 1982 (`RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID = "tests-hooks-and-orchestrator"`); line 2017 (`test_each_step_is_owned_only_by_the_heal_job`); line 2046 (`test_moved_steps_run_after_the_heal_job_setup`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The constant was retargeted to tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, but it and the two method names keep the "heal_job" wording. The docstring at lines 2000-2004 and a comment above the assignment document the move.
  WHY: There is no functional failure; a future maintainer could follow the name to the wrong job and add a step to the heal job that the contract keeps in the hooks job.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:lines 1359-1363 (the comment block above the "Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test" step in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The copied #8208 comment "This job has had no steps moved in since #7690" is false in tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, which took steps in #8278, #8993 (CHANGELOG.md line 2213) and this PR.
  WHY: CI does not break, but the stale claim misdirects the next budget-watch target choice
